PHAR 401.description: This course will provide students with a comprehensive introduction to the profession of pharmacy. It will explore the history of pharmacy and its evolving scope of practice; examine educational and career pathways; and allow students to gain insights into the regulatory and ethical considerations of pharmacy practice and more.
PHAR 401.subject: PHAR
PHAR 401.title: Introduction to Pharmacy in the United States

PHAR 402.description: This course provides students with opportunities for structured engagement and hands-on activities intended to prepare them for entry to the professional Doctor of Pharmacy degree program.
PHAR 402.subject: PHAR
PHAR 402.title: Gamecock Pharmacy Assurance to PharmD Bridge Course I

PHAR 403.description: Building upon PHAR 402 , this course provides students with opportunities for ongoing engagement and hands-on activities intended to prepare them for entry to the professional Doctor of Pharmacy degree program.
PHAR 403.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in PHAR 402.
PHAR 403.subject: PHAR
PHAR 403.title: Gamecock Pharmacy Assurance to PharmD Bridge Course II

PHAR 527.description: Conferences, assignments, and laboratory. Elective course. Contract approved by instructor, advisor, and department head is required for undergraduate students.
PHAR 527.subject: PHAR
PHAR 527.title: Problems in Pharmacy I

PHAR 700.description: This four credit hour course instructs students on the important fundamentals that define pharmaceutical sciences. Important concepts of pharmacology, medicinal chemistry and pharmaceutics are taught with the broad goal of understanding pharmaceutical agents at a molecular level. It is the introductory graduate level course for graduate students in the pharmaceutical sciences. It is also intended for graduate students in other related fields of biological, chemical, and biomedical sciences who wish to learn the principles of pharmaceutical sciences.
PHAR 700.subject: PHAR
PHAR 700.title: Principles of Pharmacology, Medicinal Chemistry, and Pharmaceutics

PHAR 701.description: Addresses recent concepts and technology in the pharmaceutical and biomedical sciences. Assists students in interpreting and evaluating published literature; and, understanding and presenting, in oral or written formats, scientific research in the pharmaceutical and biomedical sciences.
PHAR 701.subject: PHAR
PHAR 701.title: Current Topics in Pharmaceutical Sciences

PHAR 703.description: The interaction of natural and synthetic drugs with biological systems at the molecular and quasi-molecular level.
PHAR 703.subject: PHAR
PHAR 703.title: Advanced Medicinal Chemistry I

PHAR 704.description: An advanced study of natural and synthetic drugs by pharmacological classes, with emphasis on the application of principles covered in PHAR 703 .
PHAR 704.subject: PHAR
PHAR 704.title: Advanced Medicinal Chemistry II

PHAR 706.description: A study of the medicinal analyses of an advanced nature with special emphasis on instrumental methods of medicinal analysis.
PHAR 706.subject: PHAR
PHAR 706.title: Advanced Medicinal Analysis

PHAR 707.description: A study of the fundamentals of heterocyclic nomenclature and the chemistry of both the heterocyclic medicinal products and the intermediates for their synthesis.
PHAR 707.subject: PHAR
PHAR 707.title: Heterocyclic Medicinal Chemistry

PHAR 708.description: The chemistry and biogenesis of alkaloids and antibiotics.
PHAR 708.subject: PHAR
PHAR 708.title: Natural Products Medicinal Chemistry

PHAR 709.description: Lectures, seminars, demonstrations and laboratory work on recent and more technical advances in the field of biochemistry.
PHAR 709.subject: PHAR
PHAR 709.title: Advanced Biochemistry

PHAR 710.description: Lectures, seminars, demonstrations and laboratory work on recent and more technical advances in the field of biochemistry.
PHAR 710.subject: PHAR
PHAR 710.title: Advanced Biochemistry

PHAR 711.description: Discussion and presentation of current topics in pharmacy administration. Required of all master’s degree (2 credit hours) and Ph.D. degree (3 credit hours) candidates in the Department of Pharmacy Practice.
PHAR 711.subject: PHAR
PHAR 711.title: Seminar in Pharmacy Administration

PHAR 711A.description: Discussion and presentation of current topics in pharmaceutical and health outcomes research. Required of all master’s degree (2 credit hours) and Ph.D. degree (4 credit hours) candidates in the Department of Clinical Pharmacy and Outcomes Sciences.
PHAR 711A.subject: PHAR
PHAR 711A.title: Seminar in Pharmaceutical Outcomes Research

PHAR 711B.description: Discussion and presentation of current topics in Pharmaceutical Outcomes Sciences. Required of all master’s degree (2 credit hours) and Ph.D. degree (4 credit hours) candidates in the Department of Clinical Pharmacy and Outcomes Sciences.
PHAR 711B.subject: PHAR
PHAR 711B.title: Seminar in Pharmaceutical Outcomes Research

PHAR 711C.description: Discussion and presentation of current topics in pharmaceutical and health outcomes research. Required of all master’s degree (2 credit hours) and Ph.D. degree (4 credit hours) candidates in the Department of Clinical Pharmacy and Outcomes Sciences.
PHAR 711C.subject: PHAR
PHAR 711C.title: Seminar in Pharmaceutical Outcomes Research

PHAR 711D.description: Discussion and presentation of current topics in pharmaceutical and health outcomes research. Required of all master’s degree (2 credit hours) and Ph.D. degree (4 credit hours) candidates in the Department of Clinical Pharmacy and Outcomes Sciences.
PHAR 711D.subject: PHAR
PHAR 711D.title: Seminar in Pharmaceutical Outcomes Research

PHAR 712.description: Discussion of current topics in pharmaceutics, medicinal chemistry, and pharmacology. Required of all students. A maximum of 4 credit hours may be earned in PHAR 712 A-D.
PHAR 712.subject: PHAR
PHAR 712.title: Seminar in Pharmaceutical Sciences

PHAR 712A.description: Discussion of current topics in pharmaceutics, medicinal chemistry, and pharmacology. Required of all students. A maximum of 4 credit hours may be earned in PHAR 712 A-D.
PHAR 712A.subject: PHAR
PHAR 712A.title: Seminar in Pharmaceutical Sciences

PHAR 712B.description: Discussion of current topics in pharmaceutics, medicinal chemistry, and pharmacology. Required of all students. A maximum of 4 credit hours may be earned in PHAR 712 A-D.
PHAR 712B.subject: PHAR
PHAR 712B.title: Seminar in Pharmaceutical Sciences

PHAR 712C.description: Discussion of current topics in pharmaceutics, medicinal chemistry, and pharmacology. Required of all students. A maximum of 4 credit hours may be earned in PHAR 712 A-D.
PHAR 712C.subject: PHAR
PHAR 712C.title: Seminar in Pharmaceutical Sciences

PHAR 712D.description: Discussion of current topics in pharmaceutics, medicinal chemistry, and pharmacology. Required of all students. A maximum of 4 credit hours may be earned in PHAR 712 A-D.
PHAR 712D.subject: PHAR
PHAR 712D.title: Seminar in Pharmaceutical Sciences

PHAR 713.description: Application of synthetic procedures in the preparation of various medicinal and pharmaceutical chemicals and their intermediates.
PHAR 713.subject: PHAR
PHAR 713.title: Synthetic Medicinal Chemistry

PHAR 714.description: Application of molecular modeling, computer graphics, and other computational techniques to the design of drugs.
PHAR 714.subject: PHAR
PHAR 714.title: Drug Design by Molecular Modeling and Computational Techniques

PHAR 715.description: Pharmacogenomics concepts and experimental approaches combined with pharmacotherapy realms.
PHAR 715.subject: PHAR
PHAR 715.title: Pharmacogenomics and Personalized Medicine

PHAR 717.description: Lectures, readings, and discussions on special areas of experimental pharmacy not offered in other courses.
PHAR 717.subject: PHAR
PHAR 717.title: Special Topics in Pharmacy

PHAR 718.description: Lectures, readings, and discussions on special areas of experimental pharmacy not offered in other courses.
PHAR 718.subject: PHAR
PHAR 718.title: Special Topics in Pharmacy

PHAR 720.description: A study of the mathematical models used in research to describe drug changes in body fluids as related to pharmacologic effects. Includes the kinetics of dissolution, absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion after a drug reaches the general circulation. Three lecture and three laboratory hours per week.
PHAR 720.subject: PHAR
PHAR 720.title: Pharmacokinetics

PHAR 725.description: Physical, chemical, and kinetic concepts which apply to the design and evaluation of pharmaceutical systems.
PHAR 725.subject: PHAR
PHAR 725.title: Advanced Pharmaceutics I

PHAR 726.description: Application of chemical and physical concepts to the design and evaluation of pharmaceutical systems (dosage forms).
PHAR 726.subject: PHAR
PHAR 726.title: Advanced Pharmaceutics II

PHAR 732.description: The biological effects of ionizing radiation and the basic mechanisms which bring about these effects. Monitoring, dosimetry, hazard control, and legal responsibilities concerning ionizing radiation used in medicine.
PHAR 732.subject: PHAR
PHAR 732.title: Radiation Protection

PHAR 734.description: Neurochemical analysis of selected central nervous system neurotransmitter topics, including the kinetics of synthesis, storage and release, and the action of selected psychotherapeutic agents on these processes.
PHAR 734.subject: PHAR
PHAR 734.title: Selected Topics in Neuropharmacology

PHAR 735.description: The molecular and biochemical basis of cancer and the therapeutic approaches in the prevention and treatment of cancer.
PHAR 735.subject: PHAR
PHAR 735.title: Cancer: Causes, Treatment, Prevention

PHAR 736.description: Survey of drugs acting on the autonomic nervous system and the cardiovascular system; advanced topics in these areas and on antibiotics and chemotherapy.
PHAR 736.subject: PHAR
PHAR 736.title: Advanced Pharmacology I

PHAR 737.description: Survey of centrally acting drugs, anti-inflammatory and immunomodulating drugs, hormones, and vitamins; advanced topics in these areas and in drug design and drug toxicity/teratogenesis.
PHAR 737.subject: PHAR
PHAR 737.title: Advanced Pharmacology II

PHAR 738.description: Factors that govern drug response, biochemical and molecular actions of drugs, and adverse effects induced by drugs.
PHAR 738.subject: PHAR
PHAR 738.title: Basic Pharmacological Principles

PHAR 740.description: An analysis of practice environments of pharmacists. Emphasis on the drug using public and health care providers in terms of economics, social, and health factors. Detailed analysis of the third-party prescription market including prescribing behavior, drug use, cost containment, legal issues, and quality of care.
PHAR 740.subject: PHAR
PHAR 740.title: Socio-Economics of Pharmacy Practice

PHAR 741.description: Development and use of pharmaceutical outcomes databases.
PHAR 741.subject: PHAR
PHAR 741.title: Pharmaceutical Outcomes Database Development

PHAR 742.description: The nature of the research process in the administrative and behavioral aspects of pharmacy practice. Emphasis on developing the skills to analyze the total drug use process.
PHAR 742.subject: PHAR
PHAR 742.title: Research Methods in Pharmaceutical and Health Outcomes Sciences

PHAR 743.description: Basic components of a competitive grant proposal will be presented and a proposal prepared using the NIH R01 format.
PHAR 743.subject: PHAR
PHAR 743.title: Grant Writing for the Pharmaceutical Sciences

PHAR 744.description: The principles of marketing as applied to pharmaceutical products. Topics include various marketing institutions and the integration of these into the drug distribution system, and the duties of the market manager in a pharmaceutical firm.
PHAR 744.subject: PHAR
PHAR 744.title: Marketing of Drug Products

PHAR 745.description: The principles of marketing applied to the international pharmaceutical industry. Emphasis on the marketing environment and institutions of pharmaceutical marketing in global markets.
PHAR 745.subject: PHAR
PHAR 745.title: International Pharmaceutical Marketing

PHAR 746.description: Detailed analysis of the third party prescription market including prescribing behavior, drug use, cost containment, legal issues, and quality of care.
PHAR 746.subject: PHAR
PHAR 746.title: Drug Benefits in Health Care Programs

PHAR 748.description: Analytical techniques and theoretical principles for evaluating costs and consequences of pharmaceutical agents and services for the health care system and society.
PHAR 748.subject: PHAR
PHAR 748.title: Principles of Pharmacoeconomics

PHAR 749.description: Theories and methods to identify determinants, develop implementation strategies, and evaluate outcomes of evidence-based health-related programs, interventions, and policies to ensure effective, safe, equitable, and quality care.
PHAR 749.subject: PHAR
PHAR 749.title: Introduction to Implementation Science

PHAR 750.description: Didactic lectures and discussions involving content from relevant textbooks and research literature on the principles of pharmacoepidemiology, research design, and an introduction to statistical techniques used in pharmacoepidemiology.
PHAR 750.subject: PHAR
PHAR 750.title: Introduction to Pharmacoepidemiology

PHAR 896.description: Directed laboratory research and literature assignments supervised by graduate faculty.
PHAR 896.subject: PHAR
PHAR 896.title: Doctoral Directed Research
